clue.text: Fool sailor on a ship

parts.note: Jack, or Jack tar, is an old name for a sailor
SS stands for steamship, a common prefix on ships' names

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a seaman aboard a vessel as an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey-like dolt; the word is a common insult for a stupid person.

clue.text: A couple of pages to praise and praise

parts.note: p is page, so two pages are pp
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Someone heaps praise on a short piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap or commend someone is to praise them, a synonym.

clue.text: Sounding more relaxed with one's destiny

indicators.note: sounding says the word is chosen for how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: calmer means more relaxed, and in a non-rhotic accent it is said like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone sounds calmer, at peace with their fate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief, the force of past deeds shapes a person's fate.

clue.text: Firemen?

parts.note: those who feed the furnace on a steam engine or ship are firemen in a literal sense

explanation.definitionFit: On steam trains and ships the crew who shovel coal into the boiler were called firemen.

clue.text: Joint for dusting?

parts.note: a brass weapon worn over the finger joints is called a duster named after this joint

explanation.surface: A question about which body joint does the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: Dusting suggests housework, but the duster here is the brass weapon worn over the fist.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger joint is the one fitted with a brass duster, the street weapon.

clue.text: Drink specially made for the Olympics

definitions.text: Drink specially made for the Olympics

parts.words: Drink specially made for the Olympics
parts.note: the Olympians here are the Greek gods of Olympus, whose drink this was

explanation.surface: A sports drink created for the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: The Olympics suggests the Games, but it means the gods of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the gods drank this, with ambrosia as their food.

clue.text: Cautious bids ordered — it was dangerous for old sailors

definitions.text: it was dangerous for old sailors

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of the word bids are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Wary offers are placed at an auction, warning of danger at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this whirlpool faced Scylla across the Strait of Messina, a peril to Odysseus.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical whirlpool opposite Scylla menaced ancient seafarers.

clue.text: Haul on canvas that helps speed the sailor

parts.note: to lug is to haul or drag
canvas is sailcloth, so a sail

explanation.surface: Pulling on a sheet of canvas makes a ship go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-cornered sail on a yard propels a sailing boat.

clue.text: Movable feasts?

parts.note: a movable feast is a church festival with a shifting date; here it is food delivered by vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A service delivering hot food to the housebound brings the meals on wheels.

clue.text: Hits back in fight

indicators.note: back says the word for hits is read in reverse order

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: Someone strikes in return during a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To box lightly or trade practice blows is to engage in a mock fight.

clue.text: Rook in accomplished attack

parts.note: a task accomplished is over, finished
a charge is a rushing attack

explanation.surface: A chess piece features in a successful assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the chess piece but is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, as by billing too much.

clue.text: Plunder and desecrate a grave

indicators.note: desecrate suggests violating something, so the letters of the words a grave are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Grave robbers loot and violate a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to lay waste and pillage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Springtime's for female proposals

parts.note: by tradition a woman may propose marriage on 29 February, in a year read as a time for a spring or jump

explanation.surface: A remark that spring is the season when women propose marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Springtime suggests the season, but split it as spring (jump) plus time (year): the 366-day year when women may traditionally propose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition holds that women may propose on 29 February, the extra day of this calendar period.

clue.text: Commercial delegation gets right of entry

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a mission is a group of delegates sent abroad

explanation.surface: A trade delegation is granted permission to enter a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let in, or the right to be let in, is this; a synonym of entry rights.

clue.text: Like sickness benefit falsely claimed?

parts.note: benefit claimed by fraud is dishonestly obtained, and sickness benefit is got by being ill

explanation.surface: A remark about benefit fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Sickness benefit is UK state money paid to those too ill to work; split the answer as ill plus gotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Money taken by fraud is dishonestly acquired, and here the claimant pretended to be sick.

clue.text: Infantile converse

parts.note: the converse or opposite of childish is grown-up, mature

explanation.surface: Babies chatting in baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Converse looks like a verb, to chat in a childish way, but it is the noun meaning opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of infantile is grown-up, so a fully mature person.

clue.text: Gets the 1:50 in time, being nimble

indicators.note: in says the numerals go inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
1 is I and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone catches the ten-to-two train with time to spare thanks to quick feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 1:50 looks like a train time, but read it as the Roman numerals I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick and light on one's feet is a direct synonym of nimble.

clue.text: Alpine flower

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, like slow ice in the Alps

explanation.surface: A bloom found in the mountains, like edelweiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower suggests a bloom, but read it as flow-er, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowly flowing river of ice is found in the Alps.

clue.text: New pro — he wins title

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A newly turned professional sportsman wins a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: Title looks like a sports championship, but it means legal possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Title to property is legal possession of it.

clue.text: Give authority to a rising Middle East nation

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the abbreviation is read upward, so backwards

parts.note: a power is a powerful nation state

explanation.surface: Granting control to an emerging state in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise or enable someone is to vest them with power, a synonym.

clue.text: Run sail out when away from the mainland

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of run sail are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A sailor lets the sail run out when far offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or living on an island, so cut off from the mainland.

clue.text: Fuss about daughter, regarded with love

parts.note: ado is fuss or bustle
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone made a fuss over their daughter and doted on her.
explanation.definitionFit: Loved deeply or worshipped, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: What many a simpleton may do when courting

definitions.text: What many a simpleton may do when courting

parts.words: What many a simpleton may do when courting
parts.note: a noodle is a simpleton, and the answer contains a noodle that can do it: kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: An observation on how foolish people behave in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sounds like can plus noodle, a simpleton, which explains the clue's phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who are courting kiss and cuddle, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Die through his carelessness

parts.note: per means through or by, as in per post

indicators.note: carelessness suggests the letters of the word his are carelessly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is killed because of a man's negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To die, especially violently, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A trio bent on making a relationship

indicators.note: bent suggests the letters of the words a trio are twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: Three people set on forming a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between two quantities is a mathematical relationship.

clue.text: Cold buffet is a great disappointment

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold
a buffet is a blow or knock

explanation.surface: A chilly spread of food turns out to be a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet looks like a meal of food laid out, but as a noun it is also a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe setback or painful disappointment is a stock idiom for this.

clue.text: One who refused to accept tyranny to work as a bank clerk

definitions.text: One who refused to accept tyranny
definitions.meaning: William, the Swiss folk hero who defied the tyrant Gessler

definitions.text: to work as a bank clerk
definitions.meaning: a bank clerk is a teller, who counts money; to count is the old verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss archer-hero defied Austrian rule, and the verb means count, as a bank teller does.

clue.text: It should have a safety pin

definitions.text: It should have a safety pin

parts.words: It should have a safety pin
parts.note: a hand bomb is armed by pulling out its pin, so it needs one to stay safe

explanation.surface: A remark that something should be fastened with a nappy pin.
explanation.walkthrough: Safety pin suggests the clasp for nappies; here it is the pin that keeps a hand bomb from going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb has a pin that is pulled to arm it.

clue.text: Soldiers take in our weapons

indicators.note: take in says the soldiers enclose the next word

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops confiscate our arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal, a store of weapons; the word also means a collection of arms.
